title: Marriage as calling
hook: spouses become holy through each other

segments.voice: Yesterday, vocation: Samuel hearing his name in the dark, and the Church saying everyone is called to holiness. Your line was called. Which ordinary task did you do as if asked by name? Day one thousand four hundred seven.

A Catholic wedding. The priest stands at the front in white vestments, the families fill the pews, a cousin is filming on a phone. The couple turn to each other and say their vows. One detail: in the Latin Church's teaching, the priest isn't the one giving this sacrament. The bride and groom are. They give it to each other. The priest, or a deacon, is there as the Church's witness, to receive their consent and to bless them. Then everyone goes to the reception, and the couple go home, and the real work starts the next morning, with dishes in the sink. Today, marriage as calling.
screen: `A WEDDING. A PRIEST IN WHITE.` → `THE COUPLE GIVE THE SACRAMENT.` → `THEN, THE NEXT MORNING.`

segments.voice: Go back to the start of the Bible. The Lord God looks at the first man and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself." Not a servant. A help like himself. Then Paul, writing to the Ephesians, sets a very high bar: "Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the church, and delivered himself up for it." And he steps back from his own words: "This is a great sacrament; but I speak in Christ and in the church." The word Paul uses there is mystery, and the Latin Bible rendered it sacramentum. For Catholics, a marriage between baptized people is a sacrament: a sign that does what it shows. Next, the ministers. The Catechism says that in the Latin Church the spouses themselves are the ministers of the sacrament, giving it to each other by their consent. It also says the Eastern tradition sees it differently: there, the priest who crowns the couple is the minister. Both are Catholic. Then the calling. The Second Vatican Council said spouses help one another to holiness in their married life. Not in spite of each other: through each other. The person who knows exactly how you load a dishwasher, and how you sound when you're tired, is the one who gets to ask you, again and again, to forgive and to give. Every small yes in a marriage counts as part of the vocation. That's the strange claim: a marriage isn't a break from the call to holiness. It's one of the shapes the call can take.
screen: `NOT GOOD FOR MAN TO BE ALONE.` · `AS CHRIST LOVED THE CHURCH.` · `THE COUPLE ARE THE MINISTERS.` · `HOLINESS THROUGH EACH OTHER.` · then, large: `THIS IS A GREAT SACRAMENT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for a marriage. Settle, and breathe. If you're married, bring your spouse to mind, as they really are today, not at the wedding. If you're not, bring to mind a couple you know: parents, friends, neighbors, maybe a marriage that's struggling. See them at their kitchen table. If you pray, you can ask God to make them holy through each other, and name them. If you don't, simply hold them in mind and wish them patience, laughter, and one easy evening this week. The bell holds the time.
Marriage as calling. In Catholic teaching, a vocation and a sacrament in which the spouses help each other toward holiness. Today's word.

Your line: holy through each other. Today, do one unasked kindness for someone you live with or love. This week ran from processions and bells, through customs, two forms of the Mass and the renewal, into vocation and now marriage. Day one thousand four hundred seven.

howItsDone: Catholics marry in a wedding, within Mass or a liturgy of the word, where the couple exchange vows before a priest or deacon and witnesses. In the Latin Church the spouses are the ministers of the sacrament; in the Eastern Catholic churches the priest is, and he crowns the couple.

original.note: Greek, mystery: Paul's word in Ephesians 5:32, rendered sacramentum in Latin and sacrament in the Douay-Rheims.

trapdoor: what you thought: a wedding is a nice ceremony and marriage is private life.
what it means: a sacrament and a vocation, in which the spouses help each other toward holiness.
what a scholar hears: mysterion in Ephesians 5:32 becomes sacramentum in Latin; the Catechism names the spouses as ministers in the Latin Church and notes the Eastern view (CCC 1623).

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Genesis 2:18, Ephesians 5:25 and 5:32: confirm.
CCC 1623: in the Latin Church the spouses are the ministers; in the Eastern liturgies the priest is the minister, crowning the couple. Paraphrased; confirm.
Lumen Gentium 11 / CCC 1641: spouses help one another to attain holiness. Paraphrased; confirm.
Greek μυστήριον in Ephesians 5:32 rendered 'sacramentum' in the Vulgate: confirm; pronunciation given in a modern-Greek-leaning style; confirm.
'A marriage between baptized people is a sacrament' follows CCC 1601; confirm.
